findings.title: getBaseConditions can return an unparenthesized OR expression that breaks authorization when callers append AND clauses
findings.body: The org and team authorization conditions are built as `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses. The eventTypeId filter has the same shape: `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)`. `getBaseConditions` only wraps them when both auth and filter conditions exist. In the `else if (authConditions) return authConditions;` path, which is the live path when no filters are set, it returns the bare `A OR B`. A caller writing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" > ...` gets `A OR B AND C`, which SQL parses as `A OR (B AND C)`. The first branch of the authorization check then matches rows regardless of the extra filter. For an authorization predicate this is easy to get wrong silently. Wrap every returned fragment in parentheses, for example `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, or parenthesize inside the `reduce` and in each builder. The final `else if (filterConditions)` and `NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable, because `authConditions` is always a truthy `Sql` object.

findings.title: Only the user-scope path is tested end to end against the database
findings.body: `getBaseConditions` is executed with `$queryRaw` only for `scope: "user"` plus an eventType filter. The org/team scopes with `OR` combinations, `= ANY($n)` array parameters, and the combined auth-plus-filter case are only compared as SQL objects and never run against Postgres. The exact-equality tests would pass even if the SQL were invalid or had wrong precedence, for example the bare-OR problem when combined with other clauses. Add at least one execution test for org or team scope with a filter.

findings.title: Caching tests removed and new service branches left uncovered
findings.body: The "Caching" describe block was deleted, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` still exist in the service. Nothing now verifies that the second call reuses the cached value. The new `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0` and `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0` branches are also never exercised with an empty list. The team test always has a member, and there is no case for a team that is not a child of the org (`NOTHING_CONDITION`) or a team with no members. Restore the caching tests with the new `Prisma.sql` expectations and add cases for the empty-member and non-child-team branches.
